correctness.rationale: Strict singularity implies unconditional convergence, and property (V) makes the derivation weakly compact. Akemann--Wright then represents it by a c0-sum of compact-operator ideals. If a weakly compact derivation is noncompact, a nonzero component must occur on an infinite-dimensional K(H) ideal; a rank-one fiber gives a 1-complemented Hilbert subspace on which the commutator is bounded below. Thus strictly singular implies compact, and the standard compact => FSS => SS implications finish the equivalence.

originality.rationale: The consulted literature contains the weakly compact derivation structure theorem and property (V), and separately substantial strict-singularity theory for multiplication operators, but no matching compact/FSS/SS collapse for C*-algebra derivations or the c0-versus-complemented-l2 witness dichotomy was located. Older derivation and elementary-operator literature remains a documented residual risk.

value.rationale: The result sharpens the classical gap between weakly compact and compact derivations into a complete strict-singularity boundary and identifies explicit geometric witnesses for every noncompact case. The complemented Hilbert witness is reusable for commutator maps on elementary ideals.
